fixes.explanation: The Jordan it is, friend! The LORD says, “…cross over the Jordan into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.” Moses, Israel's leader, has died, and the LORD tells Joshua, “Now therefore arise, you and all these people…” Arise, and cross a whole river. I'd need a minute to stretch just to get up.

Ooh, I see why that sounds right, friend, but look at the two little words in the middle: “just as.” The LORD tells Joshua, “I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread, just as I promised to Moses.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. That promise was already made, so it's no brand new batch. It's an old recipe getting served.

Tents for the winter, friend? Now THAT is planning ahead! But winter never shows up in this message. Joshua tells the officers to say, “Prepare your provisions, for within three days you will cross the Jordan…” The people are told to get provisions ready, because the crossing is coming soon. I'd have packed the tents too, and forgotten the provisions.

Ha, that one can get you, friend! But that statement is right there in the text. Joshua tells those tribes, “Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. So True was the answer, and the little word “may” is doing the heavy lifting.
